messages.subject_clean: part5 person summary output
messages.body_plain:
Dear Vincent,

Thank you for having the new update!

I ran the GGIR script with the updated version, and I got the desired outputs for part5 day summary. However, when it came to the part 5 person summary output, it came out as one column of data..

the script that I used to run the dataset is below.. and the output that I got is attached..
Just wanted to check if I needed to add something in the script? Or wanted to check what might be the cause of this since I had managed to run the previous versions fine..

Script:

path = setwd("/Users/GGIR")
medal <- paste0(path, "/Dataset")
output_results <- paste0(path, "/Outputs")

# modify according to your analysis
part5dur <- c(1)
part2mvpadur <- c(1, 3, 5)
part1mode <- c(1, 2, 3, 4, 5)
part5mode <- c(2, 4, 5)

# version 2.0
files <- list.files(medal)
f <- files[1]

for (f in files) {
  n <- gsub(".csv", "", f)
  dir.create(paste0(path, "/Outputs/", n))
  test <- tryCatch(
  {g.shell.GGIR(#=======================================
             # INPUT NEEDED:
             mode=part1mode,# change if not need all 5 parts
             datadir= paste0(medal, "/", f),
             outputdir= paste0(path, "/Outputs/", n),
             #-------------------------------
             f0=1, f1=1,
             # Part 1:
             #-------------------------------
             # Key functions: reading file, auto-calibration, and extracting features
             windowsizes = c(5, 900, 3600), desiretz = "Asia/Shanghai",
             studyname = c("Dataset"), chunksize = 0.5,
             do.enmo = TRUE, do.anglez=TRUE,
             do.hfen = FALSE, do.hfenplus = FALSE,
             do.cal = TRUE, use.temp = FALSE,
             minloadcrit = 100, # default = 72, may need to change later
             printsummary = TRUE, print.filename = TRUE,
             overwrite = TRUE,
             selectdaysfile = c(),  # check how to use this argument
             dayborder = 0, dynrange = c(), # default = 8g

             #-------------------------------
             # Part 2:
             #-------------------------------
             strategy = 2, # may use = 3 (only select most active n days)
             hrs.del.start = 0, hrs.del.end = 0,
             maxdur = 50,   # may need to change if processing all 140 datasets
             includedaycrit = 16,
             M5L5res = 10,
             winhr = c(5,10),
             qlevels = c(0.25, 0.5, 0.75),
             qwindow=c(0,24),
             ilevels = c(0, 35,200, 707, 100000),
             mvpathreshold =c(200),
             boutcriter = 0.8,
             ndayswindow= 7, # used only when strategy = 3
             idloc = 2, # double check if can use 1
             do.imp = TRUE, # may need to change later
             storefolderstructure = TRUE,
             epochvalues2csv = TRUE,
             mvpadur = part2mvpadur,
             bout.metric = 4,
             closedbout=FALSE,
             # IVIS_windowsize_minutes and IVIS_epochsize_seconds use default 60m /3600s

             #-------------------------------
             # Part 3:
             #-------------------------------
             # Key functions: Sleep detection
             timethreshold= c(5),        anglethreshold=5,
             ignorenonwear = TRUE,       acc.metric="ENMO",
             #-------------------------------
             # Part 4: (omit for now)
             #-------------------------------
             # Key functions: Integrating sleep log (if available) with sleep detection
             # storing day and person specific summaries of sleep
             excludefirstlast = FALSE,
             includenightcrit = 16,
             #def.noc.sleep = c(),
             loglocation= c(),
             #outliers.only = TRUE,
             #criterror = 4,
             #relyonsleeplog = FALSE,
             #sleeplogidnum = TRUE,
             #colid=1,
             #coln1=2,
             #do.visual = TRUE,
             nnights = c(),

             #-------------------------------
             # Part 5:
             # Key functions: Merging physical activity with sleep analyses
             #-------------------------------
             threshold.lig = c(35), threshold.mod = c(200),  threshold.vig = c(707),
             boutcriter.in <http://boutcriter.in> = 0.9,     boutcriter.lig = 0.8,
             boutcriter.mvpa = 0.8, boutdur.in <http://boutdur.in> = c(part5dur), boutdur.lig = c(part5dur),
             boutdur.mvpa = c(part5dur),   timewindow = c("MM", "WW"),
             #-----------------------------------
             # Report generation
             #-------------------------------
             # Key functions: Generating reports based on meta-data
             do.report=part5mode,
             visualreport=TRUE,  dofirstpage = TRUE,
             viewingwindow=1
  )}, error = function(e) e)

  if(inherits(test, "error")) {
    print(paste0("File error in ", f))
    next()
  }
}

Thanks in advanced!

Regards,
Claire

Michael

messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] cut points in the algorithm?
messages.subject_clean: [GGIR] cut points in the algorithm?
messages.body_plain:
Hi Kim,

All GGIR source code is available here: https://github.com/wadpac/GGIR. All functions are documented: https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/GGIR/GGIR.pdf

GGIR facilitates a variety of ways to apply cut-points, so there is not one but multiple places where cut-points applied:
- In GGIR part 2 cut-points are used to estimate time in MVPA per 24 hours, but based on six different algorithm using a variety of epoch lengths and both with and without consider bouts. This happens in function g.analyse.perday <https://github.com/wadpac/GGIR/blob/d04fad37617a734b38d73cd0d11b72ef0eb6758b/R/g.analyse.perday.R>, lines 513 - 545, note that g.getbout <https://github.com/wadpac/GGIR/blob/master/R/g.getbout.R>, is called to do the bout detection.
- In GGIR part 5 cut-points are used in a more elaborate way, detecting also inactivity and light activity during the waking hours of a day. Here, the action happens in function identify_levels <https://github.com/wadpac/GGIR/blob/305873fd4cc6090803917cbc31bd72fadeca82c6/R/identify_level.R>, and as you will see this function also calls the g.getbout function.

Best, Vincent

Hi Maher,

Do.anglez=true generates an extra column in each the meta/basic files giving you the angleZ value per-epoch. Easy way to see if you have it already would be looking at a random .Rdata file in this folder, open it, and type “head(M$metashort)” in the console. If you have a column named “anglez” then you have the Z angle to run through part 3.

Your data directory is just the path to the folder containing the .cwa files, which you have named accordingly it seems - should be something like “E:/your Biobank folder name/cwa files”

Output directory can just be “E:/Your Biobank folder name” – This will then make the folder in the Biobank folder called “output_cwa files” which will contain all the meta files and reports too.

Ben

messages.body_plain:
Hello,

        Our research group wants to compare wrist-worn accelerometer data from Actilife using 60 second epochs, and GGIR raw epoch data (which uses 5 second epochs).

        Is one reasonable way to do this by:
1) Getting output from the  "epochvalues2csv" function
2)  Averaging all the ENMO values within a particular minute to get the ENMO value for 60 second epochs (average ENMO of 12 five second epochs).
3) Apply ENMO cutpoints (Hildebrand) to get activity classifications for each epoch.
4) Calculate how often the activity classifications differ between Actilife and GGIR across 60 second epochs.

        Thanks in advance,
        Raymond
